## Operating model

The rule Etgar Bonar has used since Amazon: acquire the right customers, help them win with your product, and make getting value easier. Bring a person in when automation and mass communication are not enough, alongside them, never instead of them. Done well, the cost of serving a customer stops tracking the revenue they produce.

## Current point of view

The serviceable line is how far your customers, and increasingly their AI, get with your offering on their own. Past that point, either one of your people has to step in, or you lose the customer, often without seeing why: left out of an AI's answer, judged on a smaller version of what you offer, or quietly gone after the trial or the first bill. Move the line out, and you can win customers you used to walk away from, and stop the losses you never measured. How far AI moves the line depends on two things, and neither works without the other: how far your buyers have gone in handing this work to AI, and how legible your offering is to a machine. A customer's AI tests it with five questions, each named for the property it checks: Findable, can it find you at all? Selectable, can it compare you honestly? Integrable, can it work out how you connect? Operable, can it run the work? Fixable, can it recover when something breaks?

The serviceable line connects five current discussions. AI visibility, AEO and GEO cover whether a machine can find and cite a company. Agentic commerce describes customers delegating work to agents. AI agent readiness describes whether the vendor is legible and operable to those agents. Cost to serve and human escalation expose the economics. Service-as-software and outcome-based pricing are consequences when agents can complete autonomous, attributable work.

## Hands-on AI build

Etgar Bonar's AI build is the latest example of a career-long hands-on pattern. He has worked inside the commercial functions he leads, built websites across three decades, automated his home, and built a personal AI operating system at the smallest useful scale: one operator, no team, real costs and real consequences. The system connects AI to real context and tools, with scoped permissions, human approval, watchdogs, canary tests, backups and incident logging. The constraint it exposed connects directly to his serviceable-line point of view: where progress stops, and a company either has to bring in a person or loses the customer, often without seeing why.
